description:
Step into a career with ASM, where cutting edge technology meets collaborative culture. ​

 For over 55 years ASM has been ahead of what’s next, at the forefront of innovation and what’s technologically possible. With more than 4,500 ASMers representing 70 nationalities, our people and our advanced semiconductor devices are playing a crucial role in trends such as 5G, cloud computing, AI, and autonomous driving.  But we’re more than just a tech company. We value diversity, inclusion and sustainability as we strive to make a positive impact on the world.  Our development programs help support your growth, shaping your future and pushing the boundaries of innovation to unleash potential.  

 

 Role Overview 

 As part of ASM's Software Engineering team, you'll develop advanced control software that powers some of the world's most sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Your work will directly support robotics, gas delivery systems, temperature control hardware, and factory automation, delivering real-time solutions that drive chip production. Based in Phoenix, you'll collaborate with global engineering teams and play a key role in shaping the future of semiconductor automation and equipment connectivity.

 Responsibilities 

 
 Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain software for semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

 Develop applications for Windows and real-time operating systems.

 Troubleshoot and resolve issues within real-time control systems.

 Diagnose and resolve software, electrical, and mechanical system issues.

 Lead technical escalation efforts with field engineers and global customers.

 Partner with Quality Assurance and Support teams to investigate issues and improve regression test coverage.

 Author and review software requirements, system specifications, design documents, and test plans.

 Investigate internal and customer-reported issues and develop effective solutions.

 Evaluate and recommend software engineering tools, processes, and best practices.

 Participate in system architecture, design, and scheduling initiatives.

 Integrate and support factory automation interfaces, including SECS/GEM and related industry protocols.

 Collaborate with automation teams to ensure reliable communication between manufacturing equipment and factory systems.

 
 Requirements 

 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.

 Strong software development experience using C#.

 5+ years of experience in software development, preferably in a full-stack or systems-focused environment.

 Semiconductor industry experience.

 Hands-on experience with factory automation systems.

 Familiarity with SECS/GEM, GEM300, and EDA (Interface A) protocols.

 Experience working with Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS).

 Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

 
 What Sets You Apart 

 
 10+ years of software development experience, including software architecture and system design.

 Experience developing machine control software, preferably for semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

 Strong knowledge of Windows and real-time operating systems.

 Experience building multi-threaded and real-time applications.

 Hands-on experience with GUI development and device drivers.

 Knowledge of networking, industrial communications, and EtherCAT.

 Understanding of dynamic scheduling algorithms and deadlock avoidance techniques.

 Ability to analyze complex system interactions and drive long-term technical improvements.

 
 
 Apply today to be part of what’s next. 

 We make the tech that enables the chips in devices which improve lives around the world. We do this with an eye to the future, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible through cutting-edge innovation, and driving the next wave of technological breakthroughs that shape how we live, work, and connect.

 To learn more about ASM, find us at  asm.com and on LinkedIn ,  Facebook ,  Instagram,   X  and  YouTube .

 
 ASM is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, nationality, social or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender, gender identify or expression, marital status, pregnancy, political affiliation, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
